metadata.description: One restart button for the DeepSeek Harness (dsh) web GUI that works with your setup: systemd, Docker, Kubernetes, pm2, launchd, terminal, Windows. Restarts in place, zero dependencies.
metadata.name: dsh-restart-anywhere

paragraphs.text: One restart button for the DeepSeek Harness (dsh) web GUI that works with your setup: systemd, Docke
r, Kubernetes, pm2, launchd, terminal, Windows. Restarts in place, zero dependencies.
A DeepSeek Harness (dsh) web GUI plugin that adds one small **Restart dsh** button above Settings. I
t is for the moments you need a restart: you installed a plugin, changed a config, or fixed a bug in
nts you need a restart: you installed a plugin, changed a config, or fixed a bug in your own plugin.
**Agents can do it too.** A `dsh_restart` tool lets an agent restart dsh after installing or editing
a plugin. With a `continue_prompt`, it is woken in the same session once dsh is back and carries on
a plugin. With a `continue_prompt`, it is woken in the same session once dsh is back and carries on.
**It works with *your* setup.** systemd, Docker, Kubernetes, pm2, a tmux pane, a plain terminal or W
indows: click, and dsh is back in a few seconds. The page reloads by itself.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## Works with your setup
Most restart buttons kill dsh and hope something starts it again. That only works for the setup thei
r author had. A detached "relaunch me" helper gets killed along with a systemd service. A clean exit
doesn't trigger `Restart=on-failure`. A container without a restart policy just stops. And under pm
2 or runit, the helper and the supervisor both start dsh and fight over the port.
dsh-restart-anywhere doesn't hand dsh's life to anyone else. It restarts dsh **in place**:
| Your setup | What happens | Leaves behind |
| **systemd** (user or system unit, any `Restart=` policy) | Asks systemd to restart the unit, so yo
u get a fresh process, exactly like `systemctl restart`. If that's not permitted (a system unit, no

root), it falls back to in-place. | nothing |
| **Docker / Podman / Kubernetes** (with or without a

restart policy) | In place: same PID, so the container never notices. | nothing |
| **pm2, superviso
rd, launchd, runit, s6, nssm, forever, …** | In place: the supervisor keeps seeing the process it st

arted, still running. | nothing |
| **Terminal, tmux, screen, nohup** | In place: same PID, and the

new dsh keeps printing to the same terminal. Ctrl-C still stops it. | nothing |
| **Windows / Node <
22.15** | Wrapper: the old process stays as a thin parent of the new dsh. It forwards Ctrl-C and ex

its with dsh's exit code. | the parent process |
| **dsh desktop app** | Button hidden: the app mana
ges its own lifecycle. | n/a |
No supervisor detection, no config, no root, no helper scripts.
## How it works
1. **Graceful shutdown.** The plugin calls dsh's own exit hook (`ctx.appExit`). Every plugin tears d

own exactly as on a normal quit, and sessions are flushed.
2. **The process becomes the new dsh.**
-
**Linux / macOS, Node ≥ 22.15:** `process.execve()` swaps the process image for a fresh dsh with th

e same command line, environment and stdio. The PID doesn't change, and nothing is left behind.
- **
Windows / older Node:** the process stays alive as a small wrapper and starts the fresh dsh as its c

hild. Later restarts reuse the same wrapper, so there's never more than one.
- **systemd:** systemd
restarts the unit itself, via a one-second transient timer, so the HTTP reply reaches your browser f

irst.
3. **The page reloads.** The browser polls until a server with a new boot ID answers, then rel
oads. That works however fast or slow the restart is.
Details that make it hold up:

- **`--port 0`:** a random port is pinned on restart, so the page finds dsh again.
- **No browser-ta

b spam:** `--no-open` is added on relaunch.
- **Double clicks:** a second request while a restart is
running gets `409`.
## Install
Into your dsh **web profile** (`web` below is the profile name; use whichever profile backs your web
GUI). From a source checkout, use `pnpm dsh` instead of `npx @deepseek-ai/dsh`:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
This installs the package into the profile and adds it to `dsh.profile.bundles`. Reload the browser
tab, and **Restart dsh** shows up above **Settings**. If it doesn't, restart dsh one last time the o
ld way. From then on, the button does it.
Requires dsh 0.2.0 or newer and Node 20+. There's no build step and no runtime npm dependencies.
## Using it
Click **Restart dsh** and confirm. The icon spins while dsh restarts, and the page reloads when the
new dsh is up, usually within about 5 seconds.
> Running agent sessions are interrupted by a restart, like with any restart. The confirmation dialo
agent sessions are interrupted by a restart, like with any restart. The confirmation dialog says so.
## For agents: the `dsh_restart` tool
Agents get the same restart as a tool, e.g. after installing or editing a plugin they want to test.

- **`dsh_restart({ continue_prompt? })`:** restarts dsh exactly like the button.
- **`continue_promp
t`:** once dsh is back, the agent is woken in the same session with this text as its next instructio

n. Leave it out and the session just stays stopped.
- **Root sessions only:** subagents don't get th

e tool.
- A wake older than 5 minutes is dropped, so a restart that never happened can't wake a sess
A wake older than 5 minutes is dropped, so a restart that never happened can't wake a session later.
## Security
- **Login required:** the restart route is registered through dsh's own `/api` connection layer (`ct
x.connection.fetch`). It only answers browsers that are logged in to your dsh, and dsh's Host/Origin

fence applies.
- **Exposed instances are safe:** on an instance reachable from the internet, an una

uthenticated request gets `401` and can't restart anything.
- **No shell commands:** nothing is run
through a shell. The only external program is `systemd-run`, and only when dsh is a systemd service.
## Tested
Verified live with dsh 0.2.0 on Linux:

- **systemd:** user unit, with `Restart=no` and `Restart=on-failure`.
- **systemd fallback:** in pla

ce, when `systemd-run` is unavailable.
- **Plain terminal:** in place via `execve`, three restarts i

n a row, then Ctrl-C and SIGTERM.
- **Wrapper path:** Node without `execve`, three restarts in a row

, then Ctrl-C.
- **Supervisor that only restarts on failure:** dsh stays up and the supervisor never

notices.
- **`--port 0`**, and two clicks at once.
- **`dsh_restart` tool:** an agent calls it with
a `continue_prompt`, under systemd and in place via `execve`. Both times it was woken in the same s
ession within seconds and finished the task. The session still reloads cleanly afterwards.
